audit_notes: Model: Couette flow in an equivalent laminar gap h with a Navier slip at the wall, u(0) = (b/h) du/dy(0), u(1) = U; wall shear tau = mu*U/(h+b). The equivalent gap h = 28 nu/u_tau = 175 um is the standard trick to reproduce a turbulent skin friction in a laminar model (h+ = U+); the slip length b = 1.9 um (b+ = 0.3) stands in for the time-averaged streamwise wall motion of an anisotropic compliant wall. Design: tau = 1.08e-3*5/(1.769e-4) = 30.5 Pa; baseline (b = 0): 30.9 Pa; gain b/(h+b) = 1.07 %. For a turbulent flow the corresponding estimate Delta U+ = b+ gives 2*0.3/28 = 2.1 %, so the Couette model is conservative by a factor 2; both hinge on the assumed b+ = 0.3, which is not derived from the layer properties (the 1D steady model cannot compute the fluid-structure interaction). Checks: natural frequency of the layer (1/t)*sqrt(G/rho) = 3.3e4 rad/s vs u_tau^2/nu = 2.6e4 rad/s, tuned; shear wave speed sqrt(G/rho) = 10 m/s vs ship speed 6-8 m/s: U/c_t = 0.6-0.8, below the static-divergence onset of elastic layers (about 2-3 c_t), but hydroelastic instabilities of soft layers at ship speed are a real risk and would increase drag. Dimensionless: h+ = 28, b+ = 0.3, U/c_t = 0.7, frequency ratio 1.27. Stress: mean wall shear 30 Pa gives shear strain 3e-4 in the layer, negligible. The auditor accepts the model as a rough bound only. Simulation coefficient: slip length 1.9e-6 m.

ui_metadata.domain_name: Turbulent skin friction over anisotropic compliant walls (Couette surrogate)

independent_var.label: Normalised distance from the wall across the equivalent gap

performance_gain.label: Skin-friction reduction vs rigid foul-release coating

hard_constraints: ship speed below hydroelastic instability onset (U/c_t < 2)

baseline_description: Rigid (non-compliant) smooth foul-release coating, no slip
